title: The 5 Longest Caves on Earth, Ranked (#2 Is Completely Flooded)

scenes.text: Number two is the longest underwater cave on Earth. Number one you can walk through.
Number five: Jewel Cave, South Dakota. About two hundred and twenty miles mapped, and still growing.
scenes.label: Jewel Cave · 220 mi

scenes.text: Number four: Sac Actun, Mexico. More than two hundred and twenty-five miles of flooded tunnels.
scenes.label: Sac Actun · 225+ mi

scenes.text: Number three: Shuanghe Cave, China. About two hundred and seventy miles, the longest in Asia.
scenes.label: Shuanghe Cave · 273 mi

scenes.text: Number two: Ox Bel Ha, Mexico. Over three hundred and twenty miles, almost all underwater.
scenes.label: Ox Bel Ha · 326+ mi

scenes.text: Number one: Mammoth Cave, Kentucky. Four hundred and twenty-six miles of mostly dry passages.
scenes.label: Mammoth Cave · 426 mi

description:
Surveyed length of the world's longest cave systems: Mammoth Cave, Kentucky, 426 miles (NPS, 2022); Sistema Ox Bel Ha, Mexico, at least 326 miles (524 km), the longest underwater cave; Shuanghe Cave, China, 439.7 km (2025 survey); Sistema Sac Actun, Mexico, more than 368 km; Jewel Cave, South Dakota, about 220 miles.
Cavers add miles to these every year, so the order can still change.
Which cave would you dare to explore?
first_comment: Which one would you put at number one if you had to explore it yourself? And what should we rank next?
